about: The sheet for the Broad Street Station cutaway: tools/cutaway/sheet.py. Callouts are anchored to drawn parts (history ids, in the isometric view and the flat section); a badge's style is the anchored part's confidence unless `confidence` says otherwise. Callout text is a working draft, written with Claude, for the artist to edit.
title: Broad Street Station, 1943
subtitle: Cut down the middle, from the Broad Street doors to the trains
sectionCaption: The same cut, seen flat: Broad Street on the left, the trains on the right

callouts.title: Broad Street
callouts.text: The front of the station, facing West Broad Street.

callouts.title: Vestibule
callouts.text: Entrance halls on each side, with stairs and elevators up to the offices.

callouts.title: White Waiting Room
callouts.text: The main hall: a low dome over a shallow vault, with four long benches.

callouts.title: Tickets, Pullman, Information
callouts.text: Counters along the east side of the hall.

callouts.title: Colored Waiting Room
callouts.text: Virginia law kept Black and white passengers apart. This wing had its own lunch room, smoking room and toilets. The waiting rooms were segregated from the station’s opening in 1919 until January 1956, when a federal order took effect.

callouts.title: Lunch room and dining room
callouts.text: In the west wing, with the kitchen behind.

callouts.title: Baggage and parcel check
callouts.text: In the east wing, off the checking lobby.

callouts.title: The concourse
callouts.text: A long room out over the tracks.

callouts.title: Stairs
callouts.text: Down from the concourse to each platform.

callouts.title: The trains
callouts.text: RF&P and Atlantic Coast Line. 33,324 passengers on April 22, 1943, the busiest day.

callouts.title: The dome
callouts.text: Tile in 1943. The copper came in 1955.

callouts.title: Offices
callouts.text: Four floors in each wing: Trainmaster, Superintendent of Telegraph, General Superintendent.

callouts.title: Basement
callouts.text: Under the whole building, on piers. It held baggage, mail and the heating plant.

key: drawn from a plan, a section or a survey map
sources: Sources: The American Architect, July 9, 1919 (text; first-floor plan, Plate 15; sections, Plates 17 and 18); Sanborn fire-insurance atlas, 1925; USGS Richmond quadrangles, 1934 and 1956; Official Guide timetables, 1933 and 1941; Richmond Railroad Museum; City Planning Commission transit map, January 1943; ICC, NAACP v. St. Louis-San Francisco Ry., 297 I.C.C. 335 (1955); OpenStreetMap.
notes: The east half of the building is lifted away down to its first floor; its walls are left standing low, as a plan. In the flat section, the departure stairs, which stand on the side lifted away, are dashed. Heights are scaled from the 1919 sections, whose figures are illegible; the first floor’s level is approximate.

and on to New York by the Pennsylvania Railroad
South by the Atlantic Coast Line to Petersburg, Charleston,
Both railroads’ trains came in and left by the north
sources: Official Guide schedules of 1933 and June 1941 (Havana Special, Tamiami Champion), as transcribed by streamlinerschedules.com

lines: To the loop, where every train turned
to leave the way it came
Streetcars and buses east to downtown
